scenes.headline: How a scrape router picks who fetches your page
scenes.sub: Five scrapers behind one endpoint, cheapest first.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Russet! Here is how a scrape router picks who fetches your page.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Put several scraping services behind one endpoint. Try the cheapest first, fall through when the site blocks it, and pay only the one that got the page.
scenes.mark: pay only the one that got the page
scenes.say: Put several scrapers behind one endpoint. Try the cheapest first, fall through on a block, and pay only the one that got the page.

steps.say: Your agent sends one address to the scrape router.
The cheapest lane tries first. Most easy pages stop right here.
If the site refuses it, that attempt is free, and the same call falls to the next lane.
Whichever lane gets the real page serves it, at that lane's price.
In the launch film, the first lane hits a four oh three. Blocked, not charged.

scenes.title: The ladder inside each vendor
scenes.say: Each vendor runs its own ladder underneath.

items.say: A plain fetch gets docs and news for almost nothing.
A headless browser renders pages that only exist after script runs.
Residential proxies change where the request seems to come from.
Unblockers bundle all of it, priced per success.

scenes.title: When does order matter?
scenes.text: cost per hit = price x P(billed) / P(hit)

parts.note: a blocked attempt is free here
parts.say: When a blocked attempt is free, the chance of being billed equals the chance of a hit.
They cancel, so the cost of a page is just the price of the lane that served it. Cheapest first is the right order.

scenes.title: 100 pages, one try each
scenes.say: On the founder's own hundred page benchmark, the router got ninety eight. Firecrawl got ninety, priced on its smallest plan.

scenes.label: Pages a ladder of the four rivals gets
scenes.say: Replay those pages through a ladder of the four rivals, and it gets ninety five. The routing does most of the work.

scenes.text: When failed attempts are free, cheapest first is the optimal order, and the router, not any one scraper, earns the extra pages.
scenes.mark: the router, not any one scraper
scenes.say: When failed attempts are free, cheapest first is the best order, and the router earns the extra pages.

recap: Cheapest lane first, fall through on a block
Pay only the lane that got the page
Rivals as a ladder get 95 of 100
scenes.say: Cheapest first, fall through on a block, and pay only for the page you got.
